title: Sections at the point commute with derived reduction modulo a power of the uniformizer
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$; put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $s=\Spec k$. Let $\Gamma(s,-)$ be sections over the final object of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ on derived categories [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. For $N\in D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], regard $\Gamma(s,N)$ as an object of $D(\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] through $\mathcal O_E\to\Gamma(s,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s})$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and let $N\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\in D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$ be the derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. Then there is an isomorphism

$$
 \Gamma(s,N)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Gamma\bigl(s,N\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\bigr)
$$

in $D(A_{E,n})$, natural in $N$, where the left side is the derived tensor product of $\mathcal O_E$-module complexes (whose restriction of scalars to $D(\mathcal O_E)$ is represented by the cone of $\varpi_E^n$ on $\Gamma(s,N)$). Consequently, for every integer $r$, $H^r\bigl(\Gamma(s,N)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\bigr)\cong\Gamma\bigl(s,\mathcal H^r(N\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})\bigr)$, $\Gamma(s,-)$ being exact.

source.place: ## Proof, Step 2 ('By def-weil-finite-coefficient-point the category D^b_c(s,A_{E,n}) is D^b_fin(A_{E,n}) ...') and Step 4 ('the uniform boundedness of Step 2 makes the O_E-cohomology finitely generated'): the passage between the integral object at the point and its finite-level reductions, used without statement; written by an agent

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $t=\varpi_E^n$, $A=R/(t)$, $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}$, and $A_s=(A_{E,n})_s$. The coefficient-ring theorem says that $R$ is a discrete valuation ring, in particular a principal ideal domain; hence it is Noetherian (each ideal has one generator). The standard quotient-resolution theorem gives $F=[R\xrightarrow{t}R]$ in degrees $-1,0$ as a finite free resolution of $A$. Apply the completed-constant-sheaf reduction theorem on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with ring $R$ and ideal $(\varpi_E)$. Its finite-resolution clause identifies $B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline F=[B\xrightarrow{t}B]$, augmented by the coefficient projection, with $A_s[0]$. Its cohomology in degree $-1$ is therefore zero and its degree-zero cohomology is $A_s$. Thus $0\to B\xrightarrow{t}B\to A_s\to0$ is exact, with the stated coefficient projection as last map. This uses completed coefficients, rather than an identification of $B$ with the discrete constant sheaf.

source.place: Tag 093M, lemma-completion-flat, applied to the two-term finite-free resolution; Tag 093J, lemma-constant-exact. The standard resolution is the integral analogue stated by lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect.

proof.text: Represent $N$ by a complex of $B$-module sheaves and choose a K-flat resolution $P\to N$ whose terms are flat, using the resolution theorem. Derived reduction is represented in $D(A_s)$ by $P\otimes_B A_s$. By the definition of flatness, tensoring the exact sequence of step 1 with each $P^j$ remains exact. Hence multiplication by $t$ is injective on $P^j$ and $P^j\otimes_B A_s=P^j/tP^j$. Locally lift $\bar b\in A_s$ to $b\in B$. The latter identification is induced by $x\otimes\bar b\mapsto bx\bmod tP^j$: two lifts differ by $tc$ and thus give the same quotient section. Its inverse is $\bar x\mapsto x\otimes1$, independent of the lift of $\bar x$ because $tx\otimes1=x\otimes t=0$. The maps commute with restrictions, are balanced, and are mutually inverse after sheafification, giving the claimed sheaf tensor isomorphism. They commute with differentials. Consequently $P/tP$ represents $N\otimes_R^L A$ as an $A_s$-complex.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; sites-modules.tex Tag 03ER, definition-flat (3); quotient identification by the balanced tensor universal property.

proof.text: The field $k$ is algebraically closed by the finite-field datum, so exactness of point sections applies to the ring sheaves $B$ and $A_s$. Put $C=\Gamma(s,P)$ and regard it as an $R$-complex through the coefficient map in the statement. Exact sections preserve the quasi-isomorphism $P\to N$, so $C$ represents $\Gamma(s,N)$. Applying exact sections to $0\to P^j\xrightarrow{t}P^j\to P^j/tP^j\to0$ shows both that $t:C^j\to C^j$ is injective and that $C^j/tC^j\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,P^j/tP^j)$. The isomorphism sends $\bar x$ to the image of the section $x$. It commutes with differentials and is $A$-linear through $A\to\Gamma(s,A_s)$. Thus $C/tC\cong\Gamma(s,P/tP)$ as complexes of $A$-modules.

source.place: Tags 0982 and 098H, lemma-w-local-strictly-henselian-extremally-disconnected and lemma-w-contractible-is-weakly-contractible; use the exact small-site sections statement already proved in lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact.

proof.text: Apply K-flat resolution on the one-point ringed site with coefficient ring $R$ to obtain a quasi-isomorphism $q:Q\to C$, where $Q$ is K-flat and every $Q^j$ is flat. The exact sequence $0\to R\xrightarrow{t}R\to A\to0$ of step 1, tensoring with $Q^j$, gives injectivity of $t$ on every $Q^j$. Here flatness means precisely exactness of this tensor functor. The ordinary reduction of $q$ is an $A$-linear chain map $\bar q:Q/tQ\to C/tC$. No K-flatness of the section complex $C$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution, on the one-point site; sites-modules.tex Tag 03ER, definition-flat (3).

proof.text: Let $T=\operatorname{Cone}(q)$, with $T^j=C^j\oplus Q^{j+1}$ and $d_T(x,y)=(d_Cx+q(y),-d_Qy)$. The quasi-isomorphism/cone criterion shows that $T$ is acyclic. Multiplication by $t$ is injective in every degree by steps 3 and 4. Finite direct sums and the displayed differential give an identification $T/tT=\operatorname{Cone}(\bar q)$ as complexes of $R$-modules (and of $A$-modules on the quotient side).

source.place: Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic, and definition-cone: cone differential and the quasi-isomorphism/cone criterion.

proof.text: Here is the elementary quotient calculation, for every integer $j$. If $\bar z\in(T/tT)^j$ is a cycle, lift it to $z\in T^j$ and write $d_Tz=tw$ with $w\in T^{j+1}$. Then $t\,d_Tw=0$; injectivity of $t$ gives $d_Tw=0$. Acyclicity of $T$ gives $w=d_Tv$ for some $v\in T^j$. Now $d_T(z-tv)=0$, so again acyclicity gives $z-tv=d_Tu$ for some $u\in T^{j-1}$. Reducing this equality modulo $t$ yields $\bar z=d_T\bar u$. Thus $T/tT$ is acyclic. This calculation has no boundedness assumption and does not assume that termwise flat complexes are K-flat.

source.place: Elementary cycle-and-boundary calculation expanding the use of Tag 05RT in the preceding step; written by the worker.

proof.text: By the cone criterion, applied now in the abelian category of $A$-modules, steps 5 and 6 show that $\bar q$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The ordinary-module derived tensor theorem, with coefficient map $R\to A$ and second factor $A[0]$, computes $\Gamma(s,N)\otimes_R^L A$ by $Q\otimes_R A=Q/tQ$. Derived reduction and exact sections compute the right side by $\Gamma(s,P/tP)$. Therefore the composite $Q/tQ\xrightarrow{\bar q}C/tC\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,P/tP)$ represents the required isomorphism in $D(A)$. In particular the morphism is constructed with its $A$-module structure, before forgetting scalars.

source.place: Tag 06Y6, lemma-derived-base-change (ordinary-module derived tensor); sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YS and 06YY; derived.tex Tag 05RT.

proof.text: Fix a flat-term K-flat sheaf model $P$ and put $C=\Gamma(s,P)$. Specialize [lem-pc-mixed-tensor-pointwise-left-derived] to $R\to A=R/(t)$ and second factor $A[0]$, using its universal derived-tensor counit $\varepsilon_C:L(Q_R C)\to Q_A(C\otimes_R A)=Q_A(C/tC)$. For a K-flat resolution $q:Q\to C$, the canonical identification is $\lambda_q=\varepsilon_Q\circ L(Q_Rq)^{-1}$. Naturality of $\varepsilon$ gives $Q_A(\bar q)\circ\lambda_q=\varepsilon_C$. Thus the first map of step 7 is independent of $q$, and its chain naturality is the naturality of $\varepsilon$. Step 7 proves this component is invertible for the particular $C$ in use. The quotient identification is the balanced map $x\otimes\bar a\mapsto ax\bmod tC$, with inverse $\bar x\mapsto x\otimes1$.

source.place: Tag 06Y6, lemma-derived-base-change and its preceding construction; counit naturality and cancellation of L(Q_R q), with the elementary tensor-quotient identification.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-derived-reduction-sheaf-resolution-independence] on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with $\mathcal O=B$, $\mathcal O'=A_s$, the map $R\to\Gamma(s,B)$ of the statement, and $t=\varpi_E^n$. Step 1 supplies its coefficient exact sequence, step 2 supplies a K-flat model with flat terms, and [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] supplies exactness on abelian sheaves. Its $\theta_P\circ c_C$ is exactly the comparison of step 7, by step 3. The lemma proves naturality for maps between such sheaf models and equality of the transported comparisons for any two resolutions of a complex $M$. Thus the comparison is independent of the sheaf model as well as of the ordinary resolution.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; strict sheaf arrow/cospan coherence extracted in the cited node.

proof.text: For a chain map $M\to M'$, [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements] supplies a strict replacement of this arrow with flat-term K-flat sources and objectwise quasi-isomorphisms. Naturality on its replaced arrow from step 9 and resolution independence give the comparison square for $M\to M'$. The functors $L\Gamma(s,-)$ and $\Gamma(s,-)T$ invert quasi-isomorphisms by the ordinary derived-tensor theorem, derived change of rings and exact point sections. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to $Q:\mathrm{CoCh}(\operatorname{Mod}(B))\to D(B)$: the chain-natural comparison descends uniquely to a natural transformation on the derived category. This includes compatibility with composition. Its components are isomorphisms by step 7, hence it is the required natural isomorphism. All replacement diagrams used here are finite, hence small.

source.place: Definition 05RU; natural-transformation descent is the existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property, clause (2), not an additional new lemma.

proof.text: To justify the cone description in the statement, restrict the left side from $A$ to $R$. In both tensor-invariance lemmas used in this step, specialize their coefficient homomorphism to $R\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}R$: the second factors $F$, $A[0]$, $Q$ and $C$ are thus ordinary $R$-complexes. In particular no $A$-module structure on the terms of $F$ is required. The complex $F=[R\xrightarrow{t}R]$ of step 1 is K-flat because it is bounded with free terms. Since $Q$ is K-flat, tensoring the quasi-isomorphism $F\to A[0]$ with $Q$ gives a quasi-isomorphism $Q\otimes_R F\to Q\otimes_R A$. Since $F$ is K-flat, tensoring $q:Q\to C$ with $F$ gives a quasi-isomorphism $F\otimes_R Q\to F\otimes_R C$. The signed interchange $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{ij}y\otimes x$ for $x$ in degree $i$ and $y$ in degree $j$ identifies $Q\otimes_R F$ with $F\otimes_R Q$. Finally $F\otimes_R C$ has degree-$j$ term $C^j\oplus C^{j+1}$ and differential $(x,y)\mapsto(d_Cx+ty,-d_Cy)$, exactly $\operatorname{Cone}(t:C\to C)$. Thus the left side, after scalar restriction, has the claimed cone representative. The actual isomorphism in $D(A)$ is the one constructed in step 7; the cone computation does not assign an ordinary $A$-action to the terms $C^j$.

source.place: Tag 064L, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side; Tag 06Y6, lemma-derived-base-change; derived.tex definition-cone. The signed tensor differential is homology.tex Tag 012Z.

proof.text: Apply $H^r$ to the isomorphism of step 7, for any $r\in\mathbf Z$. The exact-point-sections theorem, applied to the ring sheaf $A_s$ and the complex $N\otimes_R^L A$, identifies $H^r\Gamma(s,N\otimes_R^L A)$ with $\Gamma(s,\mathcal H^r(N\otimes_R^L A))$, naturally in $N$. Restriction along $A\to\Gamma(s,A_s)$ leaves this an $A$-linear isomorphism. Composing gives the last assertion, in every degree.

tool_uses.why: The integral coefficient ring is a Noetherian DVR; this is a coefficient-ring tool, not a finiteness argument. No statement of sk-lem-finite replaces this generic tool.
The two-term finite free resolution of O_E/varpi^n is the coefficient computation used in step 1. No statement of sk-lem-finite replaces this generic tool.
Its finite-resolution clause gives [B --t--> B] resolving A_s for completed, not discrete, coefficients. No statement of sk-lem-finite replaces this generic tool.
Provides unbounded flat-term K-flat resolutions on the pro-etale and one-point sites. No statement of sk-lem-finite replaces this generic tool.
Exact point sections, preservation of quasi-isomorphisms, and its cohomology formula; no node of this unit provides this site tool. No statement of sk-lem-finite replaces this generic tool.
Computes the ordinary-module derived tensor as an object of D(A), with its choice-independent comparisons. No statement of sk-lem-finite replaces this generic tool.
Finite arrow and cospan diagrams give coherent resolution choices for naturality, without changing the finiteness route. No statement of sk-lem-finite replaces this generic tool.
Choice independence and quasi-isomorphism invariance for the completed-sheaf coefficient reduction. No statement of sk-lem-finite replaces this generic tool.
The bounded two-term free quotient resolution is K-flat, used only for the cone parenthetical. No statement of sk-lem-finite replaces this generic tool.
Tensoring q:Q->C with the fixed K-flat quotient resolution preserves quasi-isomorphisms, even when C is unbounded. No statement of sk-lem-finite replaces this generic tool.

The universal ordinary mixed-tensor counit, specialized to the quotient in degree zero, supplies the augmentation and its naturality in step 8. It is generic derived-functor infrastructure, not a substitute coefficient-compatibility route.

lean.statement: theorem point_sections_derived_reduction (_hl : l ≠ D.p) (n : ℕ) : Nonempty (pointReductionTensorSections D l E n ≅ pointReductionSectionsTensor D l E n) ∧ (∀ (N : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E (Spec (.of D.k))) (C : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E))) ℤ), Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj C ≅ (pointIntegralSections l E D.k).mapDerivedCategory.obj N.obj) → Nonempty (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{u + 1, u + 1, u + 1} (pointReductionQuotient l E n)).mapDerivedCategory).obj ((pointReductionTensorSections D l E n).obj N) ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (CochainComplex.mappingCone ((ULift.up (Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E) ^ (n + 1)) • 𝟙 C)))) ∧ ∀ r : ℤ, Nonempty (pointReductionTensorSections D l E n ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ r ≅ (sfIntegralConstructible l E (Spec (.of D.k))).ι ⋙ scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E (Spec (.of D.k)) n ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ r ⋙ pointFiniteSections D.k (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))
lean.note: Index n denotes exponent n+1, covering exactly all positive exponents. The comparison is a natural isomorphism on sfIntegralConstructibleCategory with the actual derived quotient tensor in the quotient-module category. The other conjuncts explicitly give the multiplication-cone representative after restriction and the natural homology/sections isomorphism. Ordinary coefficient rings and their actions are transported only by the already recorded ULift size convention.
